title: Kathy’s Caesar Salad

items.raw: 4 cups torn country bread, in rough 1-inch pieces
4 oil-packed anchovy fillets, plus more to taste
Plenty of freshly ground black pepper
3 heads romaine, outer leaves discarded, hearts cut into 2-inch ribbons
A block of Parmigiano-Reggiano, for shaving

steps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F. Toss the bread with the olive oil, smashed garlic, and salt on a sheet pan and bake 12 to 15 minutes, tossing once, until golden and crisp but still chewy in the middle. Discard the garlic clove. Cool completely.
Mash the anchovies, garlic, and salt into a smooth paste — a mortar works best, but the flat of a knife on a board is fine. Scrape into a bowl.

Whisk in the egg yolk, Dijon, lemon juice, and Worcestershire. Then add the olive oil in a very thin stream, whisking constantly, until the dressing is thick and glossy. If it breaks, whisk a fresh yolk in a clean bowl and add the broken dressing to it slowly.

Stir in the grated Parmesan and a great deal of black pepper. Taste. It should be aggressively salty, sharp, and anchovy-forward, because the lettuce will soften all of it. Add another anchovy if it is not.
Wash and spin the romaine completely dry, then chill it. Wet leaves refuse to hold dressing and this is the reason most home Caesars are disappointing.

Put the romaine in your largest bowl. Add about two-thirds of the dressing and toss with your hands, lifting from the bottom, until every leaf is lightly coated. Add more dressing only if it needs it.

Add the croutons and toss once more. Shave a generous quantity of Parmesan over the top with a vegetable peeler and grind on more pepper. Serve at once, on chilled plates if you are being serious about it.

notes.label: About the raw egg
notes.text: for anyone pregnant, elderly, or immune-compromised, use a pasteurized egg, or substitute 3 tablespoons of good mayonnaise for the yolk and reduce the oil to ¼ cup.

notes.label: Anchovies
notes.text: do not leave them out. They read as savory depth, not fish. Two teaspoons of anchovy paste can stand in.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: dressing keeps 3 days refrigerated and croutons 2 days in a paper bag. Toss only at the last minute.

notes.label: Grilled version
notes.text: halve the romaine hearts lengthwise, brush with oil, and grill cut side down for 90 seconds before dressing.

openQuestion: Tell me a little about Kathy and this salad — is it a birthday-dinner standard, a summer thing, the salad she is always asked to bring? Also, does she use a raw egg, or mayonnaise as the base?
